# JPEG XL fixtures

Lossless JPEG XL (`1.2.840.10008.1.2.4.110`) encodes of real DICOM frames,
exercised by `packages/dicom-codec/test/jpegxl-fixtures.test.js`.

Generated by:

```
node tools/fixture-verification/gen/generate-jpegxl-fixtures.mjs [testdata-root]
```

The sources live in the separate [cornerstone viewer-testdata][testdata]
checkout rather than in this repo — the DICOM files are far too large to
vendor, and only the encoded frames are needed here. `testdata-root` defaults
to `../viewer-testdata` and can also be set with `CORNERSTONE_TESTDATA`.

[testdata]: https://github.com/cornerstonejs/viewer-testdata

## What is here

| Fixtures | Source | Geometry |
|---|---|---|
| `ct-512x512-s00.jxl` … `s15.jxl` | `dcm/scoord3d-and-scoord/scoord-bounding-box`, 16 consecutive CT slices (InstanceNumber 64–79) from the middle of a 143-slice stack | 512×512, 16-bit, `PixelRepresentation` 1 (signed), MONOCHROME2, real values in [-2048, 1704] |
| `wsi-1frame-512x512-f00.jxl` | `dcm/sm`, the single-frame whole-slide microscopy instance (`…1628847203.934`) | 512×512, 8-bit, 3 samples, interleaved RGB |
| `wsi-2frame-512x512-f00.jxl`, `…-f01.jxl` | `dcm/sm`, the first two frames of the four-frame instance (`…1628847203.933`) | as above |

The CT slices are uncompressed in the source, so their pixels are taken
verbatim. The WSI frames are JPEG baseline (`1.2.840.10008.1.2.4.50`,
YBR_FULL_422) in the source and are decoded to RGB through this repo's
libjpeg-turbo-8bit codec before being re-encoded as JPEG XL.

> **Note.** `dcm/scoord3d-and-scoord` is not tracked in the viewer-testdata
> repository, so a fresh clone of it will not contain the CT series. The
> committed fixtures and `manifest.json` are the reference; regenerating the
> CT half needs that data from wherever it originally came from.

The corpus has no two-frame WSI instance; the four-frame one is the smallest
multi-frame instance available, so its first two frames stand in. JPEG XL
carries one frame per bitstream, so a multi-frame instance is represented as
one fixture per frame either way.

## manifest.json

Records, per fixture, the frame geometry and the SHA-256 of the pixels the
bitstream must decode to. The test asserts against the manifest, so the suite
verifies these fixtures without viewer-testdata being present.

The generator refuses to write a fixture whose own decode does not reproduce
the source pixels, so a corrupt encode cannot mint its own reference.

## Signed samples and the two transfer syntaxes

JPEG XL cannot signal Pixel Representation — its sample types are unsigned
integer or float — so `jpegxl.js` picks a convention per transfer syntax, and
the CT fixtures are where that is exercised:

- **`.110` (Lossless)** hands the two's complement bits to libjxl unchanged.
  The frame round-trips byte for byte and the caller's Pixel Representation
  reinterprets it. These fixtures are all `.110`.
- **`.112` (potentially lossy)** shifts signed samples up by half the sample
  range first, because as unsigned a CT frame is two clusters either side of a
  ~62 000-count cliff that lossy coding smears across.

So a signed frame encodes to *different bytes* under the two syntaxes, and
both decode back to the identical pixels. The test suite pins that.

## The .raw references

`ct-512x512-s00.raw` (int16 little-endian) and `wsi-1frame-512x512-f00.raw`
(interleaved RGB8) are the decoded pixels of the two frames they are named
after, committed so that a regression shows up as a byte diff on real pixels
rather than only as a changed hash.
